Dondy is a Shopify WhatsApp competitor with a Built for Shopify badge, ecommerce automation, AI-related tools, integrations and a free button offering. Its Shopify integration is a real strength. The strongest WhatFlow comparison is therefore the commercial model and access to the functions the merchant needs.

A merchant begins with a free button, then wants automated messages and a usable team inbox. Compare the exact package needed for that second stage instead of assuming the free widget represents the whole automation product.

Why WhatFlow is a strong fit for store operations
WhatFlow’s all-features policy means the store chooses a plan for message volume rather than moving to a larger edition to access another feature. No seat fees apply to its team inbox.
A worked WhatFlow cost example

For a concrete baseline, consider 20,000 sent messages in a month. Among the listed WhatFlow plans, Growth produces an app-side cost of $29.00 at that volume. This calculation uses its $29.00 base, 20,000 included sends and $0.0025 rate above the allowance. It assumes a single monthly allowance and does not include tax or Meta delivery charges. It is a planning example, not a combined quote for every possible message category or destination.

Keep three lines in the budget: the application, applicable WhatsApp delivery fees, and any separate implementation or services. Meta pricing varies by destination and category, and some service or qualifying utility messages have different treatment. An app allowance does not override Meta’s rules. The current installation terms and rate pages should be checked before committing a campaign budget.
Dondy’s acquisition: what is confirmed and what to ask

Dondy announced that it joined Circeus and became part of Shop Circle in July 2026. Its announcement says the product, team, support and customer accounts would continue. The buyer has also described a broader AI-led and upmarket strategy. That is a published direction, rather than evidence that the company has no direction.

For a Shopify merchant, the useful question is how that roadmap fits the store. Ask for the current plan’s pricing, included users, support terms and the capabilities you will need next. Future commercial changes remain unknown; the acquisition alone does not establish that prices will rise or service will worsen.

If your priority is affordable Shopify WhatsApp with all features available and no inbox seat fees, WhatFlow Business API offers a clear current proposition without requiring you to buy into a broader enterprise AI program. Compare that present-day fit with the actual Dondy proposal.

This guide compares Dondy with WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API, our official Meta Cloud API app. It is separate from the older linked-device WhatFlow Chat Automation app. On October 24, 2026, Shopify showed 5.0 stars for Business API and 3.9 for the older app. Those ratings should not be combined or transferred between listings. children.text: The short answer: WhatFlow has two different Shopify apps

WhatFlow Chat Automation and WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API are separate apps from the same developer, Scrptble. The older listing is publicly named “WhatFlow: Whatsapp Automation.” It connects through the linked-device method. The newer listing, “WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API,” connects through the official Meta Cloud API. They share a brand and an ecommerce focus, but they should not be treated as the same product with one combined rating.
In this page’s comparison table, the WhatFlow column means WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API. The other column means the older Chat Automation app.
Check the
older WhatFlow Shopify listing
for its own current rating, review count and linked-device description.
Why do the two WhatFlow listings have different ratings?

WhatFlow: Whatsapp Automation is the older linked-device app at apps.shopify.com/whatflow. When checked on October 25, 2026, the listing displayed 4.0 stars from 332 reviews. It launched on October 21, 2024, giving this app a separate review history of more than two years. The comparison table retains the explicitly dated October 24 snapshot rather than treating it as the current count.

WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API has its own listing at apps.shopify.com/whatflow-official-api. It launched on May 8, 2026 and shows a 5.0-star rating from 51 reviews on the same checked date. A rating attached to the older listing should not be transferred to the separate Business API product.

The older reviews are real feedback and deserve to be read. The explanation is not that a lower rating should be ignored; it is that the buyer needs the right product name, connection method, review dates and intended workload. A newer perfect score also comes from a smaller review history. Ratings change, so the two linked Shopify listings remain the place to check the current figures.
What changed for the older linked-device product?

Our original app made Shopify WhatsApp automation accessible to merchants who wanted a low barrier to entry. A small store could connect its number through a linked device and begin with practical work such as order confirmations or fulfillment updates. For a founder handling early orders personally, that simplicity and low messaging cost could be a useful starting point.

From our team’s experience supporting merchants, the linked-device experience also became harder to rely on as WhatsApp enforcement and connection behavior changed. We saw interruptions and number restrictions affecting some stores, particularly when workloads became larger. This is our account of support experience, not an independent finding that one policy change caused every negative review. The public listing also contains connection complaints and our responses, so merchants can inspect that history themselves.

Some stores previously ran larger workloads successfully. That history does not change our current recommendation: we now position Chat Automation for small and startup stores only. “Small” is not a guarantee against restrictions, and a message being transactional does not automatically exempt the number or the sending method from WhatsApp’s rules.
What linked-device setup does and does not mean

Chat Automation’s listed connection method uses WhatsApp’s linked-device route. Its appeal is the straightforward setup and inexpensive entry point. Its suitability depends on more than order count: the number’s use, the audience, sending behavior and the consequences of an interruption all matter.

Do not decide solely by whether onboarding shows a QR code. A QR step can also appear in other WhatsApp onboarding arrangements. The important distinction is the actual integration behind it: a linked-device session versus the official business messaging platform. Ask which app is being installed and which connection method it will use.

If a small shop occasionally needs to reconnect and can handle a manual fallback, the older app may still be a practical fit. If an interruption would leave a warehouse without confirmation decisions or customers without important updates, I would choose Business API from the outset.
Compare

Why we built WhatFlow WhatsApp Business API

The newer product uses the official Meta Cloud API. It is our recommended route for stores that want a stronger operational foundation for automated business messaging. It replaces dependence on the older linked-device connection model with the official platform integration.

The Shopify experience matters just as much as the transport. WhatFlow Business API ties messaging to store events, template mapping, extensions and Shopify Flow, so an operator can work with the order behind the conversation. The team inbox helps colleagues answer the buyer after an automated update instead of leaving replies as a separate problem.

The official route still has rules. Business account eligibility, template requirements, customer permissions, message quality and WhatsApp enforcement remain relevant. Official API access does not make a number immune to restrictions or provide a promise that every message will arrive. Our recommendation is based on choosing the appropriate integration, not promising an exception to Meta’s policies.
Pricing: compare the two app bills separately

The older Chat Automation listing offers a free plan with 50 included sends and a $0.01 rate above that allowance. Its Starter is $4.99 with 1,000 included sends; Growth is $9.99 with 2,000; Professional is $14.99 with 4,000; Enterprise is $24.99 with 7,500. Those listed tiers show $0.01 above their allowances. An Ultimate subscription is listed at $49.99; confirm its current usage terms before budgeting beyond the explicitly displayed allowances.

Business API has different allowances. Its Free plan includes 100 sends, then $0.01 each. Starter is $4.99 with 2,000 sends, then $0.005; Plus is $9.99 with 5,000, then $0.004. Growth is $29 with 20,000, Scale is $49.99 with 40,000 and Ultimate is $99 with 75,000, with their respective overage rates shown on the official listing.

These are app-side prices in US dollars, billed on the listing’s 30-day cycle. Business API also needs the applicable Meta delivery charges, which depend on destination, message category and eligibility. The older linked-device app does not use the same Cloud API template-fee model. That difference can make its total sending cost attractive for modest transactional workloads, but the lower bill needs to be weighed against connection suitability.
A 5,000-message example, without hiding Meta fees

At 5,000 sends in one billing cycle, Business API Plus has a $9.99 app-side bill before applicable Meta fees and tax. In the older app, the displayed Professional allowance plus 1,000 overage sends costs $24.99; Enterprise also costs $24.99 and includes 7,500 sends. This illustrates why “the linked-device app always has the lower software bill” would be inaccurate.

The difference is $15 before Meta fees. If the Business API workload incurred $15 of Meta charges, its combined app-and-Meta amount would be $24.99 in this example. That is a break-even illustration, not a quoted Meta rate: actual country, category and eligible free-message treatment determine the real amount. Compare the full bill rather than either app’s subscription alone.

For transactional work, classification matters. A genuine order update is a different use case from a promotional offer attached to an order message. Check Meta’s current definitions and rates rather than assuming that calling a message transactional makes it free.
What Business API includes as the team grows

All WhatFlow Business API plans provide the same feature access, including Free. They differ by messaging allowances and rates. We do not make the merchant buy a higher feature edition merely to access another part of the product.

WhatFlow Business API includes an enterprise-ready team inbox without seat fees. AI is not included. All features remain available across plans, so a growing support operation does not need a higher feature edition or another per-person subscription. Theme-matched WhatsApp buttons are free forever. Free feature access and a free storefront button remain separate from automated sending costs and applicable Meta delivery fees.
Those are Business API policies. When comparing the older app, use its own current listing and configuration rather than transferring every price or entitlement from one product to the other.
How I would choose for a real Shopify store

A startup with a handful of daily orders, a tight budget and a workable manual fallback can consider Chat Automation after reviewing the linked-device tradeoffs. I would keep its purpose narrow and useful, rather than treating its low entry cost as a reason to maximize sending volume.

A store with a growing team, time-sensitive order processes or a serious campaign program should start with Business API. The official platform route, Shopify integration, included inbox and all-features model are a more appropriate foundation for the work that follows as the business grows.

Before switching an existing number, confirm its eligibility, any supported migration or coexistence arrangement and which history or settings can be retained. Test one complete journey and the human reply before cutting over. Moving to the newer app should be a planned change, not a rushed reaction to a single bad connection.

Our track record and our 2027 ambition

The newer app is a newer product, not a new team with no Shopify history. The two listings show the same developer and a merchant-facing history beginning in 2024. We want the newer Business API product to earn trust through the experience it delivers today, while learning from what merchants told us about the older integration.

My ambition is to make WhatFlow a leading choice for Shopify WhatsApp by the end of 2027. That is a goal we have to earn, not a verified forecast, a guaranteed number-one position or evidence that we are growing faster than every other app. For the merchant choosing today, the useful evidence is the correct listing, the working integration, transparent pricing and a team that explains the tradeoffs clearly.
Write the cutover acceptance criteria before moving a number

For a hypothetical migration, define the single order journey that must keep working: its template, customer permission, order reference and reply owner. Ask which number setup is supported for the actual account and which history or settings can be retained. Record those answers before changing the working connection; a QR step alone does not identify the transport behind it.

Prepare a controlled positive reply, an ambiguous answer and a repeated event for review. Keep the sample inactive while checking configuration, then plan any separately authorized delivery check. The cutover decision should depend on the supported workflow and fallback, not an assumption that a current five-star score guarantees uninterrupted operation.

Why WhatFlow is my Shopify recommendation

I would establish the official API workflow before the store becomes dependent on a linked-device session for important order updates. WhatFlow Business API combines that transport choice with Shopify events, mapped templates, Flow and a shared reply process. Keep the older app’s history visible and attributed accurately, but choose around today’s operating requirement. Confirm the supported number transition and retained settings before switching; the official foundation still requires customer permission, appropriate templates and compliance with WhatsApp’s rules.

What the current Gorgias documentation says

Gorgias documents WhatsApp conversations as helpdesk tickets. Its guide describes inbound replies, attachments, delivery status and starting a conversation with an approved template. It also explains that WhatsApp tickets can count toward ticket usage after a public agent reply.

That makes an old claim that Gorgias cannot initiate WhatsApp messages misleading. Ask to see your required template and automation in the current product, then confirm how the activity affects your account's usage.
Consult

for approved-template initiation and the public-reply billing condition.
What the WhatFlow demo makes concrete

WhatFlow places event automations and template mappings in the Shopify app. An operator can inspect an order confirmation or fulfillment template in the context of store workflows. The editor shows which Shopify field supplies each variable, which is useful when debugging the wrong name, amount or link.
This does not mean a notification solves customer support. A buyer can respond with a question that needs an agent, a warehouse check or a refund decision. Include that response in the trial.
Why WhatFlow is a strong fit for store operations

WhatFlow’s included inbox and message-based plans are easy to understand for a merchant buying WhatsApp operations. There is no additional seat subscription to add the colleague who handles delivery exceptions.
A worked WhatFlow cost example

For a concrete baseline, consider 40,000 sent messages in a month. Among the listed WhatFlow plans, Scale produces an app-side cost of $49.99 at that volume. This calculation uses its $49.99 base, 40,000 included sends and $0.002 rate above the allowance. It assumes a single monthly allowance and does not include tax or Meta delivery charges. It is a planning example, not a combined quote for every possible message category or destination.

Keep three lines in the budget: the application, applicable WhatsApp delivery fees, and any separate implementation or services. Meta pricing varies by destination and category, and some service or qualifying utility messages have different treatment. An app allowance does not override Meta’s rules. The current installation terms and rate pages should be checked before committing a campaign budget.
Classify replies before projecting the helpdesk bill

Hypothetical example: a tracking update generates a short acknowledgment, an address question and a damaged-parcel report. For each case, record whether a public agent response is sent and how the current Gorgias ticket definition applies. Keep that classification separate from the number of outbound updates and any Meta delivery charge. Do not count every incoming acknowledgment as an identical resolved case.

Compare the same response workload with WhatFlow Business API’s message plan and staffed inbox. Include a reply after a long gap so the team checks the helpdesk’s ticket-continuation rule separately from WhatsApp’s customer-service window. This produces an interpretable usage forecast without claiming that either product’s billing unit is universally better.

Gorgias may still be the right central helpdesk for a team with substantial ticket management needs across channels. That does not mean every Shopify store needs a full helpdesk purchase to start WhatsApp.
Why WhatFlow is my Shopify recommendation

Start with the useful customer conversation: a Shopify update, an appropriate reply route and a colleague who can resolve the order question. WhatFlow provides that scope without turning each participant into a seat subscription. A store with a substantial Gorgias service operation can keep it for that job. Apply the documented ticket rules to the actual response workload before budgeting, rather than treating every acknowledgment as a case or claiming a ticket and a sent message are interchangeable.
